topic: Blog share: what is sleep drive?
text:
Coffee does not remove sleepiness. It hides the signal. A new piece from psychologist Natalia Cajide explains sleep drive for a general reader.

Sleep drive is the pressure to sleep that builds while we are awake and is spent while we sleep. Adenosine is one of several signals behind it, and caffeine works by blocking the receptors adenosine acts on, so the pressure keeps building underneath.

The article also covers naps. Moving part of a night's sleep into an afternoon nap lowered the sleep pressure carried into the night, and several naps spread through a day cleared less of it than one night of sleep. In adults over 55, a review found little evidence that napping harms night-time sleep.

It closes with the heavy first half hour after waking, called sleep inertia, which can feel like proof of needing more sleep when often it is the brain coming online.

Read the full article: https://equalpsychology.com.au/blog/what-is-sleep-drive-adenosine-coffee-naps
